origin.description: Concentration of a numeric vector by the Herfindahl or Rosenbluth coefficient.
origin.usage: conc(x, parameter = NULL, type = c("Herfindahl", "Rosenbluth"), na.rm = TRUE)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Numeric vector. The measures are defined for non-negative values.

arguments.name: parameter
arguments.text: Passed to Herfindahl. NULL uses that function's default of 1. Rosenbluth ignores it.

arguments.name: type
arguments.text: Herfindahl or Rosenbluth. A unique prefix is enough. The default is Herfindahl.

arguments.name: na.rm
arguments.text: If true, drop missing values first. If false, any missing value makes the result missing.

origin.details: conc dispatches to Herfindahl or Rosenbluth. type follows match.arg, so H selects Herfindahl and R selects Rosenbluth. A NULL parameter is passed through, and Herfindahl turns that into 1, so conc(x) matches Herfindahl(x).
origin.value: A single number, the chosen concentration coefficient.
origin.example:
# generate vector (of sales)
x <- c(541, 1463, 2445, 3438, 4437, 5401, 6392, 8304, 11904, 22261)
# compute Herfindahl coefficient with parameter 1
conc(x)
# compute coefficient of Hall/Tiedemann/Rosenbluth
conc(x, type="Rosenbluth")

translation.description: Concentration of a numeric vector by the Herfindahl or Rosenbluth coefficient.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Numeric vector. The measures are defined for non-negative values. Missing values are NaN.

arguments.name: parameter
arguments.text: Passed to Herfindahl. None uses that function's default of 1. Rosenbluth ignores it.

arguments.name: type
arguments.text: Herfindahl or Rosenbluth. A unique prefix is enough, and None selects Herfindahl. Any other string raises ValueError.

arguments.name: na_rm
arguments.text: If true, drop missing values first. If false, any missing value makes the result NaN. This is na.rm in R.

translation.details: conc dispatches to Herfindahl or Rosenbluth. type follows R match.arg, so H selects Herfindahl and R selects Rosenbluth. parameter is passed through, and Herfindahl turns None into 1, so conc(x) matches Herfindahl(x).
translation.value: A single number, the chosen concentration coefficient.
translation.example:
from ineq.concentration import conc

# generate vector (of sales)
x = [541, 1463, 2445, 3438, 4437, 5401, 6392, 8304, 11904, 22261]
# compute Herfindahl coefficient with parameter 1
print(conc(x))
# compute coefficient of Hall/Tiedemann/Rosenbluth
print(conc(x, type="Rosenbluth"))
